steps.body: Three addends often total more than ten. Making the ten first turns the answer into ten-and-some, which is easy to name.
steps.narration: Three addends often total more than ten. Making the ten first turns the answer into ten-and-some, which is easy to name.

widget.prompt: The pair made ten. Now join the last addend, 6.
widget.missFeedback: Start at 10 and count on 6: you land on 16.
widget.successFeedback: Landed on 16 — ten-and-six names itself once the ten is built.

predict.prompt: Three addends of 5, 5, and 6: will the total pass ten?
predict.reveal: Two fives already reach ten, and the six pushes the total well past it.

widget.prompt: Does 6 + 4 + 4 land short of ten, on ten, or past ten?

options.label: Past ten — it reaches 14
options.feedback: Correct — the three addends together pass ten, landing on 14.

options.label: Exactly ten
options.feedback: Adding all three goes beyond ten; ten is only a stepping stone here.

options.label: Less than ten
options.feedback: Three addends this size total more than ten, not less.

options.feedback: Grouping a ten first tells you quickly that the total must be past ten.
